j.fix.NO_TIME: Do only 10 minutes today. Even 10 minutes counts.
j.fix.NO_DATA: Use radio, a library, or ask a person nearby. No internet needed.
j.fix.FORGOT: Pick one fixed time each day and tell a friend.
j.fix.AFRAID: Do it with a friend. Start with the smallest part.
j.quiet: Quiet way: send a message instead of talking.
j.talker: Talker way: do it face to face with 3 people.
j.finished2: Next: repeat it, make more, and ask for a real small job.
result.tap: Tap one to start its journey.
step.journalism.0: Listen to one radio news item. Ask: what did the reporter ask first?
step.journalism.1: Retell one thing from your village in 5 sentences.
step.journalism.2: Record a 60-second voice report about a real local issue.
step.journalism.3: Send your voice report to 5 people. Ask: was it clear?
step.journalism.4: Contact one local reporter. Ask how they got their first story.
step.repair.0: Watch someone fix a phone or radio. Ask: what did they check first?
step.repair.1: Open an old broken device and name each part you see.
step.repair.2: Fix one small fault: a loose button, a dirty charger port, or a cable.
step.repair.3: Show your fix to 3 people. Ask: would you pay for this?
step.repair.4: Visit one repair shop. Ask what they wish they knew at the start.
step.tailoring.0: Look closely at 3 clothes. Notice how seams and hems are done.
step.tailoring.1: Copy one simple seam or hem on an old cloth.
step.tailoring.2: Sew one small item: a bag, a cap, or a patch.
step.tailoring.3: Show it to 3 people. Ask: what would you change?
step.tailoring.4: Talk to a tailor. Ask how they got their first customer.
step.farming.0: Walk through a farm or garden. Notice what grows well and what does not.
step.farming.1: Plant 5 seeds or seedlings the same way a good farmer does.
step.farming.2: Look after one small plot for a week. Write what you see.
step.farming.3: Show your plot to a neighbor farmer. Ask what they would do.
step.farming.4: Ask a farmer or farm group how they sell their harvest.
step.cooking.0: Watch someone cook a dish. Notice order, timing, and taste.
step.cooking.1: Cook the same dish yourself at home.
step.cooking.2: Cook for 2 people and change one thing yourself.
step.cooking.3: Ask them: what was good, and what was not?
step.cooking.4: Ask a local cook or caterer how they price their meals.
step.hair.0: Watch a hairdresser work. Notice how they hold tools and talk.
step.hair.1: Copy one simple style on a friend or on yourself.
step.hair.2: Do one full simple style from start to end.
step.hair.3: Show the result to 3 people. Ask what they like.
step.hair.4: Ask a salon owner how a beginner can get a first client.
step.teaching.0: Watch a good teacher. Notice how they explain one hard idea.
step.teaching.1: Explain one thing you know, out loud, in simple words.
step.teaching.2: Teach one small thing to a child or friend in 10 minutes.
step.teaching.3: Ask them to repeat it. What did they understand?
step.teaching.4: Ask a teacher or tutor how they found their first students.
step.sales.0: Watch a good seller. Notice how they greet and close.
step.sales.1: Copy their greeting when you talk to someone today.
step.sales.2: Sell or swap one small thing to a person you know.
step.sales.3: Ask 3 people: why did you buy, or why not?
step.sales.4: Ask a shop owner how they find customers every day.
step.bookkeeping.0: Look at a shop notebook. Notice what is written each day.
step.bookkeeping.1: Copy one day of sales into a clean list.
step.bookkeeping.2: Keep a daily record of your own money for 3 days.
step.bookkeeping.3: Show your list to someone. Ask: is it clear?
step.bookkeeping.4: Ask a shop owner if they need help with their records.
step.webapp.0: Watch one short video on how a website is made.
step.webapp.1: Copy a tiny page: a title, a picture, and one button.
step.webapp.2: Make a one-page site about something you love.
step.webapp.3: Show it to 3 people. Ask: what is not clear?
step.webapp.4: Message a developer. Ask how they started.
step.media.0: Watch 3 videos or posters you like. Notice the light and colors.
step.media.1: Copy one photo or poster as closely as you can.
step.media.2: Make one photo, short video, or poster of your own.
step.media.3: Show it to 5 people. Ask which part they liked.
step.media.4: Ask a local photographer or designer how they get clients.
step.tourism.0: Listen to a guide or watch a tour video. Notice how they tell stories.
step.tourism.1: Tell a visitor-style story about a place you know, in 5 sentences.
step.tourism.2: Plan a 30-minute walk to show around your area.
step.tourism.3: Walk 2 friends through it. Ask what was interesting.
step.tourism.4: Talk to a local guide or hotel worker. Ask how they started.
step.interpreting.0: Listen to news in one language. Notice words you know in both.
step.interpreting.1: Say one short sentence in two languages.
step.interpreting.2: Translate one short notice or message out loud.
step.interpreting.3: Ask a friend who knows both: is it right?
step.interpreting.4: Ask someone who translates how they found their first job.
step.construction.0: Watch builders or welders at a real site. Notice the order of work.
step.construction.1: Copy one simple task with a helper: measure, mark, or cut.
step.construction.2: Build one small thing: a shelf, a stool, or a frame.
step.construction.3: Show it to 3 people. Ask what is strong and what is weak.
step.construction.4: Ask a builder or workshop owner if you can help one day.
step.driving.0: Watch a rider or driver at work. Notice how they plan the route.
step.driving.1: Learn the roads of your area. Draw a simple map from memory.
step.driving.2: Plan the best route for 3 trips around town.
step.driving.3: Show your plan to a rider or driver. Ask what is missing.
step.driving.4: Ask a rider or driver how a beginner gets work safely.
j.minor: Under 18? Go with a parent, teacher or another trusted adult. Do not meet or visit someone you do not know alone.
j.h.NO_DATA: No internet? Use radio, a library, or ask a person nearby.
j.h.NO_MONEY: No money needed. Use what you already have.
j.h.LOW_TIME: Short on time? Ten minutes is enough.
j.h.SCHOOL: Do this after school or at the weekend.
